title: Portability: Claude and Codex capability shadow matrix
description: Objective: compare the two shipped provider capability surfaces without claiming an unshipped Codex execution edge. Exercise the real durable Claude construction/dispatch evidence and the public Codex observe/probe/render/reconcile surface, reporting exact PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN per capability and platform while performing no external provider launch.
definitionOfDone: A generated matrix covers Claude and Codex on every capability both actually publish, asserts a positive row count, and identifies each result as exact PASS, FAIL, or UNKNOWN with the production reason code/layer and evidence provenance.

Claude rows use the real daemon Foundation attempt/provider construction and durable reader surface; Codex rows use only the shipped public observe/probe/render/reconcile API, and the absent production Codex execution call site is reported UNKNOWN rather than mocked or called PASS.

One accepted construction/observation control exists for each provider, while missing runtime, hostile version/output, unsupported platform, unverifiable observation, and provider-surface disagreement pin their exact production code and layer.

The matrix launches no Claude or Codex subprocess and writes no provider, activation, or attempt authority; raw event/decision/process counts and relevant filesystem bytes/mtime are unchanged before and after every arm.
All rows bind to the same checkout source commit and canonical case digest, serialize deterministically, and run under plain Node/package roots with nonzero integration-test counts.
taskRails: Use only public package roots and the real production surface under test; no test helper may reimplement a projection, provider decision, transport handshake, or host adapter.
Every refusal/failure arm asserts the exact stable reason code and refusing layer; generated matrices assert a positive case count and include an accepted control so refusal-only suites cannot pass.
All fixtures and results are advisory/read-only: no imported state may activate, mutate durable authority, select a best tool, or perform cutover.
Use TDD and mutation-drill the production surface so a named assertion reddens; keep owned files focused and stage/commit only explicit paths.
Do not claim Codex execution portability: task-2159's published observation/probe/render/reconcile capability is the Codex subject until a separate production caller lands.
No external API calls, credentials, child processes, deep imports, or caller-forged runtime/provider truth; unsupported host evidence remains UNKNOWN.
Own only the provider matrix test and at most two focused fixture/helper files under tests/integration/portability.

One ACCEPTED control: a well-formed observation/probe fixture yielding a SUPPORTED assessment with its proof method -- assert the exact CodexProofMethod member, not just SUPPORTED, because UNPROVEN_PROBE_REPORT (codex-capabilities.ts:101) exists precisely to make unproven-but-well-formed distinguishable. Hostile arms, each pinning the exact production code and layer: missing runtime, hostile version/output bytes, unsupported platform, unverifiable observation, and provider-surface disagreement (a probe report contradicting the declared capability profile). Fixtures may CREATE probe-report input records -- that is caller data the production surface validates -- but must never construct a CodexProbeReport the production validator did not accept: the forged-probe pitfall means every fixture flows through the real probe/assessment functions and the test asserts the REFUSAL when the fixture is hostile, never hand-builds the verdict object.
implementationPlan.note:
Codex rows GREEN through the bare @moe/runner root only. 36 capability rows (12 roster members x 3 platforms) plus 13 surface rows.

PLAN CORRECTION, measured in step 1 and repeated here because it changes the step text: `assessCapabilities` is NOT importable from @moe/runner. codex-surface.ts:97 says the assessment helpers stay internal, and the negative tsc probe confirmed TS2305. `probeCodexRuntime` applies assessCapabilities and capabilitySchemaDigestOf itself (codex-probe.ts:66,72), so every capability row is lifted from the profile the PRODUCTION probe built. Nothing here maps over CODEX_CAPABILITIES by hand.

ACCEPTED CONTROLS, each asserting the exact production member and not merely "it worked":
- probe-accepted-control -> profileVersion "moe-codex-capability-profile/1", provenance PROBE.
- VERSION_REPORT SUPPORTED with proofMethod exactly VERSION_RECORD, on all three platforms.
- CWD_OBSERVATION SUPPORTED with proofMethod exactly CWD_OBSERVED.
- render-accepted-control -> "moe-codex-renderer-envelope/1", provenance RENDER.
- reconcile-accepted-control -> outcome exactly PROVEN_RESULT. This one cost a real correction: my first stream fixture used a "schema" key and no terminal event, so analyzeStream classified it INCOMPLETE and reconcileCodexRun answered HONEST_UNKNOWN. The fixture now carries {"seq":1,"type":"result","subtype":"success","schemaVersion":"codex-stream-json/1"} which terminalDisposition reads as COMPLETED (codex-stream-anomalies.ts:130) and, with cancelRequested false, resolves to PROVEN_RESULT. A wrong-but-green accepted value is exactly what a refusal-only suite cannot see; this is why the control asserts the member.

A FINDING THE CONTROL EXPOSES: the accepted report carries resumeClaim "documents --resume" and RESUME still comes back UNSUPPORTED/NONE, because assessCapabilities hardcodes `record("RESUME", false, "NONE")` (codex-capabilities.ts:191). The suite asserts that explicitly - a CLAIM is not an observation, and the matrix would be lying if it credited one.

HOSTILE ARMS, each pinning the exact production code lifted from the returned value:
- probe-unsupported-platform -> CODEX_OBSERVATION_PLATFORM_INVALID (through probeCodexRuntime; platformIdentity passes straight to the builder, so no os mock is needed on this Windows host).
- observation-hostile-version -> CODEX_OBSERVATION_VERSION_INVALID. Reached through buildCodexRuntimeObservation directly, because the PROBE sanitises an unbounded reportedVersion to null via isBoundedLabel (codex-probe.ts:81) and would never surface that code.
- probe-unverifiable-observation -> port.report() throws, production falls back to UNPROVEN_PROBE_REPORT, VERSION_REPORT comes back UNSUPPORTED with proofMethod exactly NONE.
- probe-missing-runtime -> empty resolvedRuntimeClosure is VALID input; the observation answers pinningMethod UNSUPPORTED (lifted from observation.pinningMethod, vocabulary CODEX_RUNTIME_PINNING_METHODS).
- probe-surface-disagreement -> a cwdObservation whose requestedCwd and observedCwd disagree; cwdProven refuses it and CWD_OBSERVATION drops to NONE while the identical-cwd control is CWD_OBSERVED. The pair is the discriminator.
- render-context-bound-absent -> CODEX_RENDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT_UNKNOWN.
- render-authority-bearing-snapshot -> CODEX_RENDER_SKILL_SNAPSHOT_NOT_ADVISORY.

NO FORGED VERDICTS. Every fixture is caller INPUT (a probe report record, a platform declaration, a skill snapshot, raw stream bytes) that flows through the production validator; no CodexProbeReport, capability profile, rendered context or reconciliation is hand-built, and each hostile arm asserts the REFUSAL the production surface raised. The helper that builds a row from a refusal writes a sentinel ("RENDER_ACCEPTED_A_HOSTILE_INPUT" / "OBSERVATION_ACCEPTED_A_HOSTILE_INPUT") when the surface unexpectedly ACCEPTS, so a fixture that stops being hostile reddens on the vocabulary-membership assertion as well as on the exact-code one - that is drill 3's mechanism.

RENDER LAYERS ARE NOT REFUSAL LAYERS: CODEX_RENDER_LAYERS (PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS_CANONICAL/TASK_CONTEXT/SKILLS_ADVISORY) never appears in a refusedBy column anywhere in the suite.

CONSTRUCTION. createFoundationAttemptService({captureResult, store}) over SqliteEventStore.openForProject on a temp file. Row: PASS, provenance CONSTRUCTION, reasonCode DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT (vocabulary DAEMON_FOUNDATION_LAYERS), refusedBy null. Construction is evidence of construction only; the suite never upgrades it.

PLAN CORRECTION 1 - THE HOSTILE-DEPS ARM DOES NOT EXIST. The plan wanted a malformed-store-handle arm "pinning the service's own refusal". Measured: the factory body is `const { store } = deps;` (foundation-attempt-service.ts:109) and validates nothing. A malformed handle CRASHES on destructuring or later; a crash is not a refusal, and asserting on a thrown TypeError would pin no production code. Replaced with the honest equivalent that DOES pin one: dispatch-request-malformed. `dispatch(input)` calls decodeFoundationAttemptRequest on its FIRST line, before any store read and long before a launcher is prepared, so `service.dispatch({notA:"foundation request"})` returns FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_REQUEST_MALFORMED refusedBy DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT, writes nothing and launches nothing. It carries its own provenance REQUEST_REFUSAL so it can never read as CONSTRUCTION or as dispatch evidence.

PLAN CORRECTION 2 - NO SETUP SEEDING, AND NO ACCEPTED DURABLE READ. The plan wanted the scratch store seeded with "the minimal durable records the reader accepts". That is unreachable through public roots: deriveDispatchAggregateId, encodeFoundationPayload and FOUNDATION_DISPATCH_EVENT_TYPES are all absent from the @moe/daemon root (foundation-surface.ts:59-71 publishes neither), so the aggregate id cannot even be derived, let alone the canonical bytes sealed. Seeding would mean forging bytes the production codec never produced - the forged-record pitfall. The store therefore stays EMPTY and durable-read-accepted-control is UNKNOWN with unknownBecause NO_PUBLISHED_RECORD_CODEC, provenance DURABLE_READ. This makes DoD 4 stronger, not weaker: there is no setup write to be confused with an arm write. Same reasoning retires the RECORD_DRIFT arm, which needs a planted non-canonical payload at that same underivable aggregate.

DURABLE READER ARMS, each pinning code AND layer:
- durable-read-record-absent -> FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_ABSENT @ DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT.
- durable-read-identity-malformed -> FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_REQUEST_MALFORMED @ DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT (empty id).
- durable-read-store-unreadable -> FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_AMBIGUOUS @ DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT, reached by handing the reader a SECOND, genuinely CLOSED SqliteEventStore so store.readEvents throws. A real unreadable store, not a stub.

OBSERVATION. buildProviderRuntimeObservation from @moe/runner (providerId "claude"). Accepted control on all three platforms -> observationVersion exactly "moe-claude-runtime-observation/1". Hostile arms: observation-unsupported-platform -> CLAUDE_OBSERVATION_PLATFORM_INVALID; observation-hostile-version -> CLAUDE_OBSERVATION_VERSION_INVALID; observation-missing-runtime -> empty closure is accepted and truthClass comes back exactly UNKNOWN (vocabulary OBSERVATION_TRUTH_CLASSES).

UNSUPPORTED-PLATFORM ON THIS WINDOWS HOST: no os mock and no override flag was needed. platformIdentity is a CALLER-DECLARED parameter of BuildObservationInput that the production validator fences, so a hostile identity reaches CLAUDE_OBSERVATION_PLATFORM_INVALID / CODEX_OBSERVATION_PLATFORM_INVALID for real. The three well-formed platform declarations (darwin-arm64, linux-x64, win32-x64) are likewise caller data, never a claim about the running host.

THE WITHHELD CLAUDE SURFACES, all UNKNOWN and all asserted against the RUNTIME barrel namespace rather than a comment: probeClaudeRuntime, renderClaudeContext, assessCapabilities and recordClaudeStream are absent from Object.keys(import * as runnerRoot from "@moe/runner"), so capability-probe is PROVIDER_ASSESSOR_WITHHELD, context-render is PROVIDER_RENDERER_WITHHELD and run-reconciliation is PROVIDER_STREAM_RECORDER_WITHHELD (reconcileClaudeRun IS published but needs a ClaudeStreamRecord no published recorder can produce). implementationPlan.description: Mutation drills, three, one per load-bearing distinction. Drill 1 (provenance honesty -- the prior architect's central pitfall): relabel the Claude CONSTRUCTION row's provenance as dispatch-grade evidence (or upgrade its verdict from the construction fact to an execution PASS); a NAMED test must go RED on the provenance/verdict assertion. If nothing reddens, the matrix is not actually asserting provenance per row and step 2 must be strengthened. Drill 2 (roster coverage is real): remove one capability's row generation for one provider; the per-provider row-count-equals-roster-length assertion must go RED naming the count, and the missing-capability set assertion (roster minus covered) must name the capability. Drill 3 (refusal arms test production, not fixtures): make one hostile Codex fixture VALID (so the production surface accepts it); the arm's exact-code assertion must go RED because the refusal it pins no longer occurs -- proving the arm exercises the production validator rather than asserting on fixture shape. Record command, failing test NAME, exact assertion for each. Restore by re-editing, never `git checkout` (shared worktree), confirm `git diff --numstat` 0/0 per drilled file, one drill at a time.

planningNotes.risks: The load-bearing risk is evidence-class laundering: a green construction call or a parsed render output quietly upgraded into execution evidence -- exactly what the prior architect's pitfalls forbid ('do not label service factory construction as dispatch evidence', 'do not treat render layers as refusal layers'). The closed provenance column plus drill 1 make that laundering a named red instead of a silent upgrade. Second, forged Codex truth: a hand-built probe report or capability profile asserts provider facts nobody observed; every fixture must flow through the production probe/assessment path, and drill 3 proves the hostile arms exercise the production validator rather than fixture shape. Third, the read-only invariant must hold on FAILURE paths too -- hostile arms are where stray writes hide, so the count/mtime capture wraps every arm, not just the controls. Fourth, roster drift: the matrix must derive rows from the imported frozen rosters, never a transcribed list, or a capability added later silently gets no row; the row-count-equals-roster-length assertion plus drill 2 pin it. Fifth, determinism: timestamps, Map iteration order, and per-row HEAD reads are the three usual nondeterminism leaks in a matrix serialization -- read the commit once, sort canonically, no clock anywhere. Sixth, the unsupported-platform arm on a Windows-only host: honesty beats coverage -- an os mock is caller-forged runtime truth, so without a public platform-override parameter the row is UNKNOWN with provenance stated. Seventh, tests/integration is typechecked by nothing by default and test:integration's chained legs each need their own read of the output. Finally, close every scratch store handle on every path -- a held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker.
